checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in TX
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Type I commercial exhaust hood listed/labeled per UL 710 with NFPA 96 compliance and building department-approved capture velocity per IMC 507
ANSUL R-102 (or equivalent UL 300) hood suppression: post-install discharge test certificate + every-6-month cleaning + annual inspection per NFPA 96 §11
ANSUL discharge auto-shutoffs all hood gas + electric fuel sources per IMC 507.7 — use the listed building department source during witness test
Grease interceptor sized per IPC 1003.3.4 by drainage fixture units (4-comp + mop typically 50+ GPM hydromechanical OR 750–1,500 gal exterior gravity); located ≤25 ft developed length from fixtures
Makeup air system balanced to ±10% of hood exhaust per IMC 506.3.4; tempered if > 35°F differential to prevent backdraft
ADA fixture counts per IBC Table 2902.1 + 60 in turning radius + lavatory pipe wrap insulation per ADA §606.5 + mirror reflective edge ≤40 in AFF per ADA §603.3
Local health department food establishment plan review + final inspection sign-off REQUIRED before Certificate of Occupancy (parallel filing — file early)
Walk-in cooler envelope per IECC 403.10.1 (≥R-25 medium-temp panels, ≥R-32 freezer panels); door gasket seal verification at final
Existing sprinkler system reuse: hydraulic recalc for new layout + current 5-year cert per NFPA 25; new heads in cooking equipment area must be K-25+ per NFPA 13
Floor drains within 5 ft of kitchen equipment per IPC 411 with backwater valves where required
Fire alarm + emergency lighting per NFPA 72/101 with current battery capacity test on file
Change of occupancy memo (B/M → A-2): include occupant load + exits + restroom count + sprinkler/fire-alarm impacts per IEBC §1001.2/1001.3 + IBC §303.3 (Group A-2)

Maricopa County (or local equivalent) Environmental Services Department food-establishment plan review + final inspection sign-off REQUIRED before opening — coordinate with City CO schedule (MCESD: maricopa.gov)
Outdoor patio / sidewalk dining: verify city zoning (use permit may apply, e.g. Phoenix ZO §1207); include patio in occupant load + exiting + accessible route + sprinkler/awning review

Phoenix-specific (or equivalent local rule): contractor must be AZ ROC licensed AND associated with the Phoenix SHAPE PHX permit account before submittal (A.R.S. Title 32 Ch. 10) — frequently-missed pre-submittal blocker

Realistic fee warning: a 3,200 sq ft restaurant TI in Phoenix typically lands $8K–$25K+ across plan review + permit + fire + utility + health + zoning. Reject token min-fee outputs; calculate from the live fee schedule before quoting

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Commercial trade contractors pull their own permits in Houston using their state license credentials: the Texas licensed plumber pulls the plumbing permit, the TACL-licensed HVAC contractor pulls the mechanical permit, and the fire suppression contractor pulls the fire permit. Houston does not require a separate city contractor license, but the contractor's license number must appear on the application.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to Houston Permitting Center (HPC)

common_mistakes: Submitting the restaurant TI as a single trade permit instead of a commercial building permit plus the required plumbing, mechanical, and fire suppression permits
Forgetting the grease interceptor permit or undersizing the interceptor for the kitchen fixture load
Installing hood suppression without a separate fire permit and final acceptance test
Missing gas appliance venting, combustion air, or make-up air details on the plan set
Starting work before plan review approval and permit issuance
Assuming Houston city rules apply everywhere in the metro area — some addresses in unincorporated Harris County may have different permit handling, so verify the exact jurisdiction before filing

pro_tips: For Houston commercial TI work, submit a complete plan set the first time: hood, suppression, grease interceptor, gas piping, and equipment schedules all need to line up or plan review will bounce it.
Bring the project valuation breakdown with labor and material numbers ready; valuation-based fees move faster when the reviewer can see the scope clearly.
If the suite is in a flood-prone area, check whether Harris County Flood Control District review or additional drainage requirements apply before you finalize the kitchen layout.
Have the fire suppression contractor coordinate with the hood installer before submittal so the suppression nozzle locations and hood dimensions match the approved drawings.

what_to_bring: Completed commercial tenant improvement permit application and project address
Stamped plan set showing floor plan, hood layout, grease interceptor details, gas appliance schedule, and suppression system layout
Contractor license numbers and expiration dates for plumbing, HVAC/mechanical, and fire suppression trades
Equipment cut sheets for hood, exhaust fan, make-up air unit, grease interceptor, and all gas appliances
Tenant lease or owner authorization letter for the suite
Project valuation breakdown for the $260,000 scope
response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Houston has no zoning, so HOA/zoning-style use restrictions are usually not the issue inside the city. For a commercial restaurant, the bigger blockers are occupancy classification, fire code, grease interceptor sizing, and any lease or shopping-center landlord design criteria. If the suite is in a historic district or subject to deed restrictions/private covenants, those can still delay exterior work or signage, but they usually do not control the interior permit itself.
